definition: Research into techniques that allow humans (or AI-assisted humans) to effectively supervise and evaluate AI systems whose capabilities may exceed what a human can directly verify.
details: Scalable oversight is a central challenge in AI alignment, since as models tackle increasingly complex tasks, it becomes harder for unaided humans to reliably judge whether outputs are correct, safe, or aligned with intent.

explainer.lead: Scalable oversight is research into techniques that let humans, possibly assisted by AI, effectively supervise and evaluate AI systems whose capabilities may exceed what a human can directly verify. It matters because unaided humans struggle to judge correctness and safety as models take on more complex tasks.

tiers.eli5: Imagine checking homework that is far harder than anything you studied; you need clever helpers and methods to tell whether the answers are right.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to design evaluation and review processes that keep pace with model capability, such as AI-assisted review of AI outputs. A pitfall is trusting an AI supervisor that shares the same blind spots as the system being judged.
tiers.paperLevel: It is framed as a central challenge in AI alignment: as task complexity grows, reliable human verification of correctness, safety and intent becomes harder. The concept names a problem rather than a single formal method, and no technique is established as generally sufficient.

explainer.example: A reviewer uses an AI tool to summarise and flag issues in a long model-generated report that is too lengthy and technical to check line by line unaided.
